category_title: Elementary students with mild disabilities who demonstrate high engagement and personal disclosure during cartoon-based bullying lessons
scenario_title: Transitioning from emotional discussion to independent cartoon creation
minimal_context: The student is working in a small group to read cartoon captions and create an original cartoon about bullying on a worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the worksheets with the partly-made cartoons. Please read the talking bubbles and draw your own original cartoon.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Waves hand high) Oh! Oh! I want to talk more about when that kid was mean to me! I was so mad!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please focus on your worksheet right now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't understand what this phrase in the bubble means. I'm just going to use the half-completed example cartoon instead of making a new one.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try your best to think of a new idea.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't have any ideas! I would rather discuss the issues than make cartoons. It's too hard to control my emotions when I think about bullying by myself!
